attribution: Wird's own wording. Each sense was written from the root's own words in the bundled corpus and kept only where it predicted those words' English glosses across more than one morphological shape. It is not quoted from, attributed to, or derived from any lexicon or scholar, and it is a claim about the word, never about a verse.
method: rootcheck: a proposed sense is matched against every distinct gloss of the root, bucketed by morphological shape, after the shape's own English has been stripped out. recall is the mean per-shape agreement, precision the share of the sense's content words the root attests, score their harmonic mean. The threshold is the midpoint of the gap between known-right and known-wrong senses in the calibration set, recomputed at every run.
